claims.text: The starting material is a NbMoTaW refractory high-entropy alloy without a pre-existing protective surface scale.
The proposed intervention is deposition of an approximately 50 nm Al2O3 coating by atomic layer deposition.
An intermediate graded layer is included to improve coating adhesion and accommodate thermal-expansion differences.
The ALD process will produce a highly dense, conformal Al2O3 barrier on NbMoTaW.
A dense Al2O3 layer can physically separate an alloy substrate from oxygen and inhibit further oxidation.
The proposed 50 nm Al2O3 coating will minimize oxygen ingress into NbMoTaW and prevent its rapid oxidation at 1200°C.
The graded adhesion layer will mitigate thermal-expansion mismatch and reduce coating cracking or spallation during prolonged high-temperature exposure.
The coating will improve the oxygen resistance of NbMoTaW during exposure at 1200°C in pure oxygen at 1 atm for 10 hours.
Coated NbMoTaW will have a lower oxidation rate and lower weight gain than uncoated NbMoTaW under the stated exposure conditions.
Coated NbMoTaW will exhibit less oxide-scale disruption or spallation than uncoated NbMoTaW.
Untreated NbMoTaW will rapidly form non-protective, spalling oxide scales at 1200°C in pure oxygen.
Untreated NbMoTaW will consequently show greater weight gain and poorer surface integrity than coated NbMoTaW.
Residual stress or coating defects could limit oxidation protection if the graded layer and deposition parameters are not properly optimized.
Performance under thermal cycling or exposures substantially longer than 10 hours remains unvalidated.
The magnitude of the expected oxidation-resistance improvement has not been quantitatively established.
